findings.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites in `GetObjectInfo`, at reporter lines 735, 1009 and 1101. The diff guards only two of them: the hunks at new lines 985 and 1077 correspond to reporter lines 1009 and 1101 at the same -24 offset. Nothing touches the earlier site near reporter line 735 (about line 711 now). The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper only filters a Diagnostic after it is built. It cannot stop an `IndexOutOfRangeException` thrown while computing the location argument. If that third site is reached for the metadata `Item<T>`, the generator (CS8785) and the analyzer (AD0001) still crash.

findings.claim: The change also suppresses an error diagnostic for types declared in the compilation itself. `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null when the property's declaring syntax is not a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. A positional record parameter declared with `[property: Key((string)null)]` is such a case: its syntax is a ParameterSyntax. The resulting null-location `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` diagnostic is then dropped by `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, because `Location.None.IsInSource` is false. So the error is silently lost for a type declared in this project. That contradicts the requirement that same-assembly types keep their diagnostics and that only metadata symbols lose them.
